title: Myths About the Body
objective: After this level you can debunk common myths, like using only 10 percent of your brain.
summary: No 10% brain, no tongue map, no swallowed spiders, no growth after death, no heat-leaking head. One-hand knuckle tests and blinded sugar trials show how evidence wins.

cards.headline: Seven things 'everybody knows' about the body. All seven are wrong.
cards.body: Here's how people found out, from brain scans to a doctor who spent 50 years cracking the knuckles of just one hand.

items.label: The 10% brain
points: Brain scans find no completely silent area
Damage to almost any area has lasting effects

items.label: The tongue map
points: A 1901 study found only tiny sensitivity differences
A 1940s redrawing turned them into separate zones
Every area with taste buds senses every taste

cards.headline: The doctor who cracked one hand
cards.body: Does knuckle cracking cause arthritis? Donald Unger tested it on himself. For 50 years he cracked the knuckles of his left hand at least twice a day, leaving the right as a control. In 1998 he reported no arthritis in either hand, and won an Ig Nobel Prize for it in 2009. One man proves little, but a 2011 study of 215 people found hand arthritis about as common in crackers as in non-crackers.

items.label: Spiders in your sleep
points: Your heartbeat and breathing send out warning vibrations

items.label: Hair and nails after death
points: Drying skin pulls back, so they only look longer

items.label: Heat lost through the head
points: The head is about 10% of your surface
Heat loss tracks how much skin is uncovered

cards.headline: The sugar rush that wasn't there
cards.body: Double-blind trials find sugar doesn't change children's behavior or thinking. So why do parents see it? In a 1994 study, every boy got a sugar-free placebo, but some mothers were told their sons had been given sugar. Those mothers rated their sons as more hyperactive. The sugar rush was in the watching.

mascot.line: Level 96's placebo effect again, this time fooling the grown-ups doing the watching.

cards.headline: Myths: busted
learned: You use far more than 10% of your brain
No tongue map; spiders avoid sleepers
Hair and nails don't grow after death; the head is no heat leak
Knuckle cracking and sugar myths fail the evidence test

questions.prompt: What did Donald Unger find after cracking only his left hand's knuckles for 50 years?

options.label: Arthritis in the left hand only
Stronger knuckles on the left
options.rationale: He reported no difference between hands.

questions.explanation: Unger reported in 1998 that neither hand had arthritis and there was no apparent difference between them.

questions.prompt: Why can a dead person's hair and nails look longer, even though they have stopped growing?

options.label: Growth hormones keep working for weeks
options.rationale: Growth needs hormonal control that stops at death.

options.label: The skin dries and pulls back around them
Cold makes hair and nails expand
options.rationale: Drying skin, not cold, explains it.

options.label: Nails keep taking in water
options.rationale: The skin loses water; nothing is added.

questions.explanation: Drying skin retracts, exposing more of the hair and nails, which creates the illusion of growth.

questions.prompt: From Level 55: brain scans busted the left-brain, right-brain myth. What do scans show that busts the '10% brain' myth?

options.label: The unused 90 percent is in the cerebellum
options.rationale: Nobody has found an unused 90 percent anywhere.

options.label: No brain area is completely silent
Only the left half is active at rest
options.rationale: Neither side dominates; scans found no lopsided people.

options.label: Children use far more of it than adults
options.rationale: No scan found an unused part at any age.

questions.explanation: Just as scans found no left- or right-brained people, they find no completely silent area of the brain.
